citations.quote: Would activities that an RA 13 depositary performs in its capacity as a Transfer Agent (TA) (eg, processing payments in designated accounts) be subject to requirements under the CMR?
only when such LC is not acting as a Transfer Agent

In such cases, the depositary is expected to observe relevant requirements under Schedule 11 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Schedule 11), in particular paragraphs 9 (relating to how subscription and redemption proceeds should be held) and 11 (relating to distribution proceeds).

readings.distinction: Activity-specific attachment: the negative qualification concerns the LC’s capacity in the relevant transaction. This reading is preferred because Q1 expressly asks about activities performed in a particular capacity. Schedule 11 expectations remain a separate question; their satisfaction is not a conjunct of the CMR antecedent.

citations.quote: The CMR will apply to an RA 13 licensed corporation (LC) and its associated entity (AE) in respect of “scheme money” received or held in Hong Kong by the RA 13 LC or its AE in the course of conducting Type 13 regulated activity by the RA 13 LC, only when such LC is not acting as a Transfer Agent.

readings.distinction: Corporation-wide attachment: “such LC” makes the LC’s concurrent Transfer Agent activity a restriction on the whole applicability statement. This is textually plausible because the answer does not expressly say “in respect of that money,” although the activity-specific wording of the question weighs against it. Unlike the first reading, unrelated concurrent Transfer Agent work defeats the antecedent.
